state.body: packages/agentchat/test/worker/shutdown.test.ts:179 does readFileSync("packages/agentchat/bin/agentchat-worker.ts") — a path relative to the process cwd, not the package. Running the worker suite as `cd packages/agentchat && bun test test/worker` fails exactly one test (createWorkerShutdown > worker signal handlers catch shutdown rejections before exiting) with ENOENT and reports 657 pass / 1 fail; the same suite from the repo root (`bun test packages/agentchat/test/worker`) is 658 pass / 0 fail. Observed 2026-09-01 on the post-land gate for 533b1c5d (Task A retry fence), which had zero shutdown/signal changes. Rule: every fleet check and maestro gate runs `bun test <package path>` from the repository root; never cd into a package first. A zsh side-trap in the same gate: `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is bash-only — zsh uses `$pipestatus[1]`, so the pipeline exit code read 0 while the suite was red.

state.body: In zsh, `path` is the special array tied to $PATH. A `while read path` (or `for path in ...`) loop assigns it and destroys PATH for the rest of the compound command — and because zsh runs the LAST pipeline segment in the current shell, the damage persists past the loop: every later git/wc/tr call fails "command not found". Bit the 2026-08-27 pm-3 GC sweep: all `git worktree remove` calls inside the loop failed as WT-FAIL and the cleanup silently did nothing. Same hazard for other zsh special names (cdpath, fpath, manpath). Fix: never use `path` as a shell variable — use wt/dir/p2; each Bash tool call gets a fresh shell, so recovery is just re-running with a safe name.

state.body:
Measured 2026-08-27: a penumbra-fix-until-green check shaped `bun test <files> 2>&1 | tail -5 && bunx tsc --build` returned process exit 0 on a run whose tail printed `5 fail` — tail's exit masks bun's, so the loop's PASS/FAIL judgment silently inverts. The worker itself caught it only because it re-ran unmasked; a less careful implementer would have shipped on a fabricated green.

Rule: compose check commands as `bun test <files>; echo bun_exit=$?; bunx tsc --build; echo tsc_exit=$?` and have the worker judge the echoed codes. Same rule for review prompts ("report actual output — no tail/head pipes"). Companion bun facts still true: bun 1.3.14 can panic AFTER printing the summary (parse counts, not raw exit), and `tail -8` capture loses the real numbers ([[reconciler-baseline-no-node-modules-root-cause-confirmed-2026-08-17]]).
